preamble: Change of the palatal glide /j/ to the lateral approximant /l/. It is attested in Central Papuan Oceanic languages of south-east New Guinea: Proto-Oceanic *y between /a/ vowels appears as l in Motu (POc *puqaya 'crocodile' > huala, *maya 'tongue' > mala) and in East Mekeo (ufala 'crocodile'). It is not regular in every environment (POc *kayu 'tree' > Motu au), and a sporadic parallel is Numbami a-mala 'tongue'. No well-documented case outside Oceanic has been verified.

examples.note: Most Oceanic reflexes keep the glide or lose it (Dobuan, Roviana mea).
Irregular in Numbami: yuwaya 'seahorse' (< *puqaya) keeps y.
